default_port_notes.8429: vmagent HTTP (also VMSingle on operator deployments per upstream issue #1343)

misconfig_patterns: Default deployment exposes :8428 with no auth; all metrics read + query without credentials
Write surface (/api/v1/import, /api/v1/import/prometheus) accepts unauthenticated writes by default — allows metric injection / data corruption
Admin endpoints (/api/v1/admin/tsdb/delete_series, snapshot/create) protected only by -deleteAuthKey / -snapshotAuthKey if set; default empty allows authenticated-equivalent admin
/debug/pprof/ exposed by default even with -httpAuth set (per upstream issue #3060) — leaks runtime state and stack traces
vmui (web UI) at /vmui/ runs queries against the same unauth API surface
/api/v1/status/tsdb reveals series counts, label cardinality, churn rate — operator workload size inference
/api/v1/label/__name__/values returns FULL list of metric names — perfect schema-disclosure for operator profiling
Cluster mode (vmstorage/vmselect/vminsert) exposes 8480/8481/8482 with no auth; vminsert accepts unauth writes from anywhere

active_probe.false_positive_check: response body must include the literal string 'VictoriaMetrics' AND a 'version' field starting with 'v'; Prometheus also exposes /api/v1/status/buildinfo with similar shape, so the brand-name string is the discriminator

fingerprint_oracle.discriminator: VictoriaMetrics returns top label-value-count series with seriesCountByMetricName, seriesCountByLabelValuePair; Prometheus returns headStats + seriesCountByMetricName but different envelope

deployment_tells: vmui SPA at /vmui/ identifies VictoriaMetrics uniquely (Prometheus has no equivalent UI bundled)
Metric names with vm_ prefix (vm_rows, vm_data_size_bytes, vm_app_uptime_seconds) in /metrics output
/metrics output includes 'vm_app_version' label with VictoriaMetrics build info
pivot_paths: GET /api/v1/label/__name__/values -> full metric-name catalog -> operator stack inference (e.g., 'kube_pod_*' means K8s, 'kafka_consumer_*' means Kafka, 'mysql_global_*' means MySQL)
GET /api/v1/series?match[]={__name__=~'.+'} -> full series catalog with labels -> per-target hostname/instance disclosure
GET /api/v1/query?query=up -> currently-monitored targets with up/down status -> production-instance inventory
GET /api/v1/status/tsdb -> top series by label-value-pair -> highest-cardinality workload signatures
POST /api/v1/import (unauth write surface) -> inject arbitrary metrics; corrupt monitoring / poison alerting
POST /api/v1/admin/tsdb/snapshot/create -> trigger filesystem snapshot (DoS via disk fill)
vulnerabilities: CVE-2025-65942 (GHSA-66jq-2c23-2xh5): Snappy decoder ignores request size limits, malformed block triggers OOM DoS on write path. Affects <1.110.23, 1.111.0-<1.122.8, 1.123.0-<1.129.1; patched 1.110.23/1.122.8/1.129.1. Reachable via the unauth /api/v1/import write surface = remote unauth DoS.
Issue #3060: -httpAuth flags do not apply to /debug/pprof/ — auth bypass on profiling endpoint reveals runtime internals
Design choice (NOT a CVE): no authentication on default deployment; documented in upstream SECURITY.md as 'operator responsibility' to deploy vmauth or restrict network access
Metric injection via /api/v1/import (unauth write): attacker forges metrics, poisons SLO / autoscale / alert systems downstream
auth_default_thesis: AUTH-OFF-DEFAULT confirmed: VictoriaMetrics ships with no -httpAuth set; operators must explicitly add auth or run behind vmauth proxy. Per upstream docs 'By default, port 8428 is not protected in any way nor is encrypted.' Direct analog to ChromaDB's posture: open by design, auth is the operator's job.
research_questions: What share of internet-exposed VictoriaMetrics has /api/v1/import accepting writes without auth? (population-scale write-surface metric)
What share has /debug/pprof/ exposed regardless of -httpAuth setting? (the upstream issue #3060 pattern)
How does VictoriaMetrics population auth-on-default rate compare to Prometheus (the platform it's replacing)?
What operator-attribution signal can be extracted from /api/v1/label/__name__/values catalogs at scale? (the 'metric-names-as-org-chart' pretext-payload hypothesis)
